lessons.title: Say how long and how long ago
lessons.summary: Say you've lived here for three years, arrived three years ago, or worked somewhere for a while: {{depuis}}, {{il y a}} and {{pendant}}.
lessons.topic: {{depuis}} + the present ({{j'habite ici depuis…}}); {{il y a}} + a length of time (ago); {{pendant}}; {{ça fait … que}}

goal.t: J'habite à Paris depuis trois ans. Je suis arrivée il y a trois ans, en juin.
goal.tr: I've lived in Paris for three years. I arrived three years ago, in June.

dialog.t: Vous avez mal depuis quand ?
dialog.tr: How long have you been in pain?

dialog.t: Depuis trois jours.
dialog.tr: For three days.

dialog.t: Et vous avez de la fièvre ?
dialog.tr: And do you have a fever?

dialog.t: Oui, depuis hier soir. J'ai pris un médicament il y a deux heures.
dialog.tr: Yes, since last night. I took some medicine two hours ago.

dialog.t: D'accord. Vous allez prendre cet antibiotique pendant une semaine.
dialog.tr: OK. You're going to take this antibiotic for a week.

blocks.p: **Depuis + the present.** For something that started in the past and is still going on, French uses the **present** with {{depuis}}: {{J'habite ici depuis trois ans.}} “I've lived here for three years” (and I still do). English says “I have lived”; French says “I live here since three years”.

{{Depuis}} covers both “for” (a length of time) and “since” (a starting point): {{depuis deux heures}} “for two hours” or “since two o'clock”, {{depuis 2020}}, {{depuis lundi}}. To ask: {{Depuis quand … ?}} or {{Depuis combien de temps … ?}} “How long…?”
**Il y a: ago.** With the passé composé, {{il y a}} + a length of time means “ago”: {{Je suis arrivée il y a trois ans.}} It's the same {{il y a}} as “there is”, used another way.
**Pendant: for a finished stretch.** For something that lasted a while and is over, use {{pendant}}: {{J'ai habité à Rome pendant deux ans.}} “I lived in Rome for two years” (and then I left).

table: I've worked here for five years.
{{J'ai commencé il y a cinq ans.}}
{{J'ai travaillé à Lyon pendant cinq ans.}}
I worked in Lyon for five years.

blocks.p: **Ça fait … que.** In speech, {{ça fait}} + a length of time + {{que}} is another way to say {{depuis}}: {{Ça fait une heure que j'attends !}} “I've been waiting for an hour!”

ex.tr: I've been waiting for you for twenty minutes!

ex.t: Tu apprends le français depuis combien de temps ?
ex.tr: How long have you been learning French?

ex.t: J'ai vu Paul il y a deux jours.
ex.tr: I saw Paul two days ago.

ex.t: Nous avons attendu pendant une heure.

ex.note: word for word “it makes a long time”

blocks.tip: {{Depuis}} with a negative passé composé says how long something hasn't happened: {{Je n'ai pas mangé depuis ce matin.}} “I haven't eaten since this morning.”

mistakes.wrong: J'ai habité ici depuis trois ans.
mistakes.tr: I've lived here for three years.
mistakes.why: Still true now: {{depuis}} with the present.

mistakes.wrong: Je suis arrivé depuis deux jours.
mistakes.right: Je suis arrivé il y a deux jours.
mistakes.why: “Ago”, a moment in the past: {{il y a}}.

practice.why: A stretch of time that's over: {{pendant}}.

lessons.title: Say what just happened and what's happening right now
lessons.summary: Say you've just arrived, you're in the middle of cooking, or you're about to leave: {{venir de}}, {{être en train de}} and {{être sur le point de}}.
lessons.topic: {{venir de}} + infinitive (just done); {{être en train de}} + infinitive (in the middle of); {{être sur le point de}} (about to)

goal.t: Je viens d'arriver à la gare. Tu es où ?
goal.tr: I've just arrived at the station. Where are you?

dialog.t: Allô ? Tu es où ?
dialog.tr: Hello? Where are you?

dialog.t: Je viens de sortir du bureau. Et toi ?
dialog.tr: I've just left the office. And you?

dialog.t: Je suis en train de faire les courses pour ce soir.
dialog.tr: I'm in the middle of doing the shopping for tonight.

dialog.t: Super. Les invités vont arriver à huit heures ?
dialog.tr: Great. Are the guests going to arrive at eight?

dialog.t: Oui, et Paul vient d'appeler : il apporte le dessert.
dialog.tr: Yes, and Paul just called: he's bringing dessert.

blocks.p: **Just done: venir de + infinitive.** {{Venir}} “to come” + {{de}} + an infinitive says something has only just happened: {{Je viens de manger.}} “I've just eaten.” The verb is in the present, but it means the very recent past (word for word, “I come from eating”).

**Right now: être en train de + infinitive.** French has one present for “I work” and “I'm working” (lesson 13). To stress that something is going on at this very moment, say {{être en train de}}: {{Je suis en train de travailler.}} “I'm (busy) working.”

**About to: être sur le point de.** {{Aller}} + infinitive (lesson 19) says what's going to happen; {{être sur le point de}} says it's going to happen any second: {{Le train est sur le point de partir.}} “The train is about to leave.”

table: {{Je suis sur le point de manger.}}

blocks.p: **In a story**, {{venir de}} and {{être en train de}} go into the imparfait (lesson 28): {{Je venais de rentrer quand tu as appelé.}} “I had just got home when you called.” {{J'étais en train de dormir.}} “I was sleeping.”

ex.t: Chut, le bébé est en train de dormir.
Tu es en train de lire quoi ?
Le film est sur le point de commencer.
ex.tr: The movie is about to start.

blocks.tip: {{Je viens de…}} is the French for “I've just…”. Don't translate “just” with {{juste}}: {{J'ai juste mangé}} means “I only ate”.

mistakes.why: After {{venir de}}, the infinitive ({{-er}}), not the participle.
“Just”, for something very recent, is {{venir de}}.

mistakes.right: Je suis en train de travailler.
mistakes.why: Don't forget {{de}}: {{en train de}}.
